page: Microsoft Azure F80amds_v7 is an AMD-powered compute and memory-dense virtual machine within the Famdsv7 series, operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is driven by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz across 80 dedicated physical cores and 80 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware acceleration features include vector and cryptographic instruction sets such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions, AES, and SHA-NI. The server is configured with 640.0 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per core ratio, and includes 9,449 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results place the processing and memory subsystems consistently within the top tier. In stress-ng evaluations, the server achieves top-decile ratings in both single-core (3,787.88) and multi-core (289,014.91) compute workloads. Memory throughput is equally robust, reaching 467.51 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 209.76 GB/sec on large-block writes. Data processing pipelines benefit from high-throughput compression metrics, such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 1,067.64 GB/sec. Although lacking discrete GPU acceleration, the 80-core EPYC architecture delivers competitive CPU-based LLM inference, reaching 5,858.1 tokens per second on small 135M parameter prompt processing and 62.22 tokens per second on medium 7B text generation.

The combination of dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores, massive RAM allocation, and 9.4 TB of high-speed local NVMe storage establishes strong resource efficiency for infrastructure consolidation. The instance reduces CPU scheduling contention while delivering top-tier performance in database operations (39,850.54 in PassMark) and in-memory key-value processing, evidenced by 196.41 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. The lack of complimentary public IPv4 addressing and discrete accelerator hardware requires external network configuration and rules out GPU-bound model training. The instance is suited for high-throughput in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, intensive compression or ETL workloads, and high-concurrency static web serving.
description: Microsoft Azure F80amds_v7 is a dedicated high-capacity virtual machine built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 80 physical cores across 80 vCPUs with 1:1 hardware thread mapping, supported by 640.0 GB of memory and 9,449 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the instance achieves top-decile performance across multi-core compute, uncached memory bandwidth, and high-rate compression. In-memory datastore evaluations demonstrate extreme throughput, logging 196.41 million operations per second in Redis SET workloads alongside strong CPU-based LLM prompt processing. While the absence of discrete GPUs limits dedicated deep learning training, the large memory footprint and massive fast local storage provide high density and efficiency for database servers, large-scale caching layers, data engineering pipelines, and demanding web infrastructure.
